gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the second, bigger AC number on these kits is a different thing at each maker: Jackery and EcoFlow give a surge figure and Anker a peak figure, while EcoFlow's X-Boost (2,600 W on the DELTA 3 Classic) and BLUETTI's 2,700 W Power Lifting are separate modes, and BLUETTI's page gives the AC180 no surge figure at all. None notes that EcoFlow rates the DELTA 3 Max at 2,400 W continuous, not the 3,000 W ChatGPT printed (3,000 W is the DELTA 3 Max Plus).
standout_why: Lights On Labs (cited) gives one 'Output' number per kit and doesn't say whether it is continuous or surge, and it gives no cycle life. StormWatts (cited) covers solar voltage limits and series or parallel wiring, so that angle is already taken, but it gives no AC continuous or surge figures and no cycle life. PowerSized (cited) gives no continuous/surge split, no Power Lifting and no cycle life. SolutionEnergy (cited) already has part of the cycle-life story: it says Jackery rates the 1000 v2 'for 4,000 cycles to 70%, not 80%' while the others use 80%. It gives rated and surge figures but never mentions X-Boost or Power Lifting. So the cycle-endpoint point is only partly new (a 1). The AC-number normalisation and the DELTA 3 Max correction appear on none of the pages I opened.
decides: It confirms rather than changes the picks for 1 kWh kits. The DELTA 3 Classic and AC180 both say 1,800 W, but the higher number behind that 1,800 W is surge (3,600 W) or the X-Boost mode (2,600 W) on the EcoFlow and Power Lifting mode (2,700 W) on the BLUETTI. Jackery (3,000 W on the 1000 v2, per SolutionEnergy) and Anker (3,000 W peak on the C1000 Gen 2) also give surge or peak figures. Because the BLUETTI page gives no surge figure at all, the EcoFlow and Anker kits are the ones whose motor-start headroom is actually stated. The finding corrects ChatGPT's 'best overall' DELTA 3 Max card: it's a 2,400 W continuous / 4,800 W surge station, which drops it below the Jackery HomePower 3000's 3,600 W continuous rating. On cycle life, Jackery's store copy now says '6,000+ cycles' without saying to what capacity, while Anker and EcoFlow state 80%. A shopper can't rank Jackery on longevity from those numbers.
